headline: Failed House rule would have set debate terms for a defense spending bill, a natural gas trade bill, and a resolution criticizing New Mexico's governor.
what_it_does: This was a procedural resolution, called a "rule," that would have set the terms for House debate and votes on three other measures. Those were H.R. 4365, which would fund the Department of Defense for fiscal year 2024, and H.R. 1130, which would repeal certain limits on importing and exporting natural gas, including limits tied to free trade agreements. The third was H.Res. 684, which would condemn New Mexico Governor Michelle Lujan Grisham's actions restricting firearms. The rule itself would not have changed any law; it only would have allowed those measures to come to the floor under set procedures.

who_it_affects.group: Members of the House of Representatives
who_it_affects.how: They would have debated and voted on the three measures under the procedures and time limits this rule set.
